title: DNS Gateway fields in the DNS log: slot, server protocol and flags

prose.text: Three fields carry the DNS Gateway outcome. {{dnsgw-slot-proto}} The DNS Insights Logs article describes the Resolver Gateway column differently {{divergence:resolver-gateway-meaning}}. The column text is in [[zia.logs.dns-outcome:resolver-gateway-column]].

prose.label: Flags.
prose.text: {{dnsgw-flag-glosses}} {{failure-behavior-options}} [[zia.dns-control.gateways:failure-behaviors]] Whether the flags are exclusive, their order and how they map to the failure behavior are open {{gap:dnsgw-flags-semantics-open}}.
The general outcome fields are in [[zia.logs.dns-outcome]] and naming in [[zia.logs.dns-record-fields]].

checks.do: Which glossed meaning the dnsgw_flags value carries, and whether failover behavior is configured on the gateway.
Whether one record can show several flags, before filtering on equality.

dnsgw-slot-proto.statement: The dnsgw_slot field is the name of the DNS Gateway rule, shown in Insights as Resolver Gateway, and dnsgw_srv_proto is the DNS Gateway server protocol, with TCP, UDP and HTTP as examples.

quotes: | %s{dnsgw_slot} | The name of the DNS Gateway rule | DNS GATEWAY Rule 1 | Resolver Gateway
| %s{dnsgw_srv_proto} | The DNS Gateway server protocol | TCP, UDP, HTTP | Server Protocol
If applicable, the DNS fields are mapped to their corresponding columns in DNS Insights Logs (Data Explorer > Internet & SaaS > DNS Insights > Logs).

dnsgw-flag-glosses.statement: The NSS DNS log output format page glosses the dnsgw_flags values as PRIMARY_SERVER_RESPONSE_PASS for Primary Server Attempted, SECONDARY_SERVER_RESPONSE_PASS for Secondary Server Attempted, FO_DEST_PASS for Query Forwarded to Destination, FO_DEST_ERR for Error Response Returned to Client and FO_DEST_DROP for Query Dropped, with None also listed.

quotes: | %s{dnsgw_flags} | Flags indicating the DNS Gateway status for the transaction | PRIMARY_SERVER_RESPONSE_PASS (i.e., Primary Server Attempted) SECONDARY_SERVER_RESPONSE_PASS (i.e., Secondary Server Attempted)
FO_DEST_PASS (i.e., Query Forwarded to Destination) FO_DEST_ERR (i.e., Error Response Returned to Client) FO_DEST_DROP (i.e., Query Dropped) None | DNS Gateway Flags |

failure-behavior-options.statement: The Cloud & Branch Connector help gives a DNS gateway's failure behavior as either Return error response or Forward to Original DNS Server.

quotes: The failure behavior for the gateway (i.e., **Return error response** or **Forward to Original DNS Server**).

resolver-gateway-meaning.summary: The NSS DNS output format describes dnsgw_slot as the name of the DNS Gateway rule, mapped to the Resolver Gateway column, while the DNS Insights Logs article describes Resolver Gateway as the resolver used and a separate DNS Gateway Flags column as the request status at the gateway level.

quotes: | %s{dnsgw_slot} | The name of the DNS Gateway rule | DNS GATEWAY Rule 1 | Resolver Gateway |

positions.says: dnsgw_slot is the name of the DNS Gateway rule and maps to the Resolver Gateway column.

quotes: Resolver Gateway: The name of the DNS resolver (primary or secondary, within the configured DNS Gateway of the triggered rule) that was successfully used to resolve the DNS request or displays the error resolution, if any.
DNS Gateway Flags: The DNS request status at the DNS Gateway level.

positions.says: Resolver Gateway is the name of the primary or secondary resolver that resolved the request, or the error resolution, and the gateway-level status is the separate DNS Gateway Flags column.

resolver-gateway-meaning.impact: Whether the Resolver Gateway value is a rule name or a resolver name depends on which page is read; dnsgw-slot-proto states the NSS side.

dnsgw-flags-semantics-open.title: Whether dnsgw_flags values are exclusive and how they map to gateway failure behavior
dnsgw-flags-semantics-open.blocks: diagnosing why a gateway DNS query failed
dnsgw-flags-semantics-open.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the CSV does not expand "FO", does not say whether values are one per record or cumulative, does not give the transition order between primary, secondary and FO_* states, does not distinguish when FO_DEST_ERR fires versus FO_DEST_DROP, and does not say when None appears. Whether FO_DEST_ERR and FO_DEST_DROP correspond to the gateway failure behaviors is not stated (legacy clarification log-16).
